teams.heading: Fiji seek to improve performance following November 2025 defeat against France
teams.body: Fiji look to reverse their form in the upcoming Round four fixture against France. In their last meeting with Les Bleus, which took place in November 2025 during an international friendly, Fiji suffered a 34-21 away defeat. The Flying Fijians currently sit 12th in the 12-team Nations Championship table, having failed to secure a victory in their opening three matches. Their Round three fixture ended in a 17-33 defeat against Scotland. Across these three tournament appearances, Fiji have scored 49 points. They have also conceded 145 points.

teams.heading: Steve Borthwick seeks national team progress from £264m Premiership club agreement
teams.body: Two years after the Rugby Football Union signed a £264m Professional Game Partnership with Premiership clubs, Steve Borthwick's England side has yet to see the expected benefits on the international stage. With the next World Cup only 12 months away, questions remain over the national team's progress under the deal. Although the agreement allows Borthwick to award 25 enhanced player contracts to gain greater squad control, the actual level of influence remains highly debated while domestic clubs continue to prioritise their own commercial recovery.

lead.why: It addresses the structural debate surrounding Borthwick's squad control and the £264m Premiership partnership ahead of the upcoming World Cup.

teams.heading: France national team secure 54-12 away victory against Wales in February
teams.body: The France national team recorded their largest margin of victory in their last 11 matches during the 2026 Six Nations. The side defeated Wales 54-12 in an away fixture in February 2026, marking the highest points total achieved in the current window. Across these 11 games, France have scored a total of 426 points and conceded 291. This represents an average of 38.7 points scored and 26.5 points conceded per match.

teams.heading: Ireland Women back row Aoife Wafer ruled out of Japan fixture
teams.body: Aoife Wafer is ruled out of Sunday's Ireland Women fixture against Japan in Galway after sustaining a minor injury during training. Head coach Scott Bemand has responded by making six changes to the starting XV following a loss to the United States. Brittany Hogan joins the back row, while Eilís Cahill earns her first international start. Bemand noted that the encounter offers an "ideal opportunity" to develop the squad's attacking prowess during this World Cup cycle.

lead.why: A significant injury to a key back-rower and a reshuffled matchday squad for the ongoing WXV competition.

teams.heading: Italy Men sit 11th in Nations Championship after 10-57 Australia defeat
teams.body: Italy Men currently sit 11th in the Nations Championship table after three rounds of competition. The side has conceded 131 points across their opening fixtures, leaving them with a points difference of -94. This total was heavily impacted by a 10-57 away loss to Australia in July 2026. That result marked a fourth consecutive defeat for Gonzalo Quesada's team, who have secured one victory in their last five international outings.

teams.heading: Scotland Women host Australia in Edinburgh seeking first WXV Global victory
teams.body: Scotland Women host Australia this afternoon aiming to recover from successive WXV defeats against Canada and New Zealand. While the hosts have recorded 40 points across their opening two fixtures, they remain winless heading into the final match of the first Global Series block at the Edinburgh Rugby Stadium. Australia are also searching for their first win of the campaign, having struggled through the opening weeks. The match will be available to stream via BBC iPlayer as Scotland seek to conclude their home fixtures with a victory.

teams.heading: Deian Gwynne named potential World Cup bolter amid difficult Wales season forecast
teams.body: Gloucester back-rower Deian Gwynne has been identified as a surprise contender for the senior squad ahead of next year’s World Cup. The former Wales U20 captain, currently playing in the Gallagher Premiership, is viewed as a potential bolter for Steve Tandy’s side during a season that includes the upcoming Nations Championship. Forecasts suggest Wales face a battle to avoid a fourth successive Six Nations wooden spoon following recent heavy defeats to Argentina and South Africa on the summer tour.

teams.heading: Argentina conclude latest home international window with 28-28 draw against Australia
teams.body: Argentina concluded their latest international window with a 28-28 draw against Australia at home this month. This result contributes to a recent run of form that has seen Los Pumas record one win, three losses and one draw across their last five matches. In the current Nations Championship table, the side sits in eighth position after three rounds. The squad heads into the upcoming November fixtures having scored 97 points while conceding 99 in the tournament so far.

teams.heading: Lukhan Salakaia-Loto replaces injured Josh Canham for South Africa Test match
teams.body: Australia have been forced into a late pack reshuffle after lock Josh Canham was ruled out of the Perth Test with a hamstring injury. Head coach Les Kiss has promoted Lukhan Salakaia-Loto to the starting XV to replace the lineout caller, with Lachlan Shaw joining the replacements. Captain Harry Wilson noted that Salakaia-Loto’s physicality will be vital against a world champion side that has made 13 changes, as the Wallabies look to sustain their recent form under the new coaching regime.

lead.why: The Canham injury is a late material change to the starting line-up that was not covered in previous editions.

teams.heading: Japan Women seek tactical response against Ireland in Galway WXV encounter
teams.body: The Japan Women's national side aim to overcome a seven-place ranking deficit when they face Ireland at Dexcom Stadium this weekend. Following a period where the team has struggled for form, the Japanese must counter an Irish side bolstered by six personnel changes. Ireland head coach Scott Bemand noted Japan’s "certain style" as a specific challenge, while tactical analysis suggests the visitors must prioritise a disciplined opening 40 minutes to neutralise the hosts’ proven early-game potency.

teams.heading: Scott Barrett returns for Taranaki following Ardie Savea permanent captaincy appointment
teams.body: Scott Barrett returns for Taranaki against Hawke’s Bay this weekend following a 10-month absence due to a bulging disc and surgery. The lock revealed that head coach Dave Rennie contacted him to confirm Ardie Savea would take over as permanent captain for the Nations Championship. Barrett, who has 89 caps, admitted that the recent coaching change from Scott Robertson to Rennie was personally challenging. He now aims to "give everything I've got" to earn a recall after proving his fitness in the National Provincial Championship.

lead.why: Barrett is returning to action for Taranaki while providing his first public comments on losing the captaincy to Ardie Savea.

teams.heading: Springboks Prospect Andre-Hugo Venter Excels During Stormers United Rugby Championship Victory
teams.body: Stormers hooker Andre-Hugo Venter earned man-of-the-match honours following a standout performance in his side’s 29-15 United Rugby Championship win over Connacht in Galway. The rookie Springbok was instrumental in the visitors' forward effort, covering 71 metres with ball in hand and completing 17 tackles. His high-impact display, which included a contribution to a solid scrum platform, underscored his growing reputation as the Cape side secured a bonus-point victory away from home.
